claim_text: GCN propagates features with the renormalised adjacency D~^{-1/2} A~ D~^{-1/2} where A~ = A + I, so neighbour weights are fixed by node degrees rather than learned.

The GCN paper states its approximations assume locality and equal importance of self-connections and neighbour edges, and that the framework is limited to undirected graphs without native edge features.
The GCN paper reports Cora as 2,708 nodes, 5,429 edges, 7 classes, 1,433 features and label rate 0.052, following the Planetoid setup (20 labels per class, 500 validation, 1,000 test nodes).
GAT computes attention e_ij = LeakyReLU(a^T [W h_i || W h_j]) with negative slope 0.2 and normalises with a softmax over j in N_i, the first-order neighbourhood including node i itself.
In GAT the coefficients are normalised per target node, so for every node i and every head the coefficients over its neighbourhood sum to 1; summing them at a fixed target is therefore constant.
source_location: Sec. 2.1, Eq. 2 (consequence derived from the softmax definition)

claim_text: GAT concatenates K heads in hidden layers and averages them in the final prediction layer.
The GAT transductive setup used 8 heads of 8 features, ELU, dropout 0.6 on layer inputs and on the normalised attention coefficients, and reached 83.0 +- 0.7% on Cora versus 81.5% for GCN.
GAT supports directed graphs by omitting alpha_ij when the edge j -> i is absent.
The GAT authors only suggest that analysing learned attention weights may help interpretability; they do not validate attention as an explanation.
GATv2 changes the scoring to e(h_i, h_j) = a^T LeakyReLU(W [h_i || h_j]), applying the attention vector after the non-linearity.

A GAT layer computes only static attention: the ranking of neighbours is the same for every query node, and only the sharpness of the distribution depends on the query; GATv2 computes dynamic attention.
GATv2 was more robust than GAT to random structural (edge) noise on ogbn-arxiv and ogbn-mag.

DOMINANT uses a shared GCN encoder with a GCN attribute decoder and a structure decoder that reconstructs the adjacency by an inner product of node embeddings, and scores nodes by reconstruction error.

claim_text: In the official PyTorch implementation the per-node score is alpha times the L2 attribute reconstruction error plus (1 - alpha) times the L2 structure reconstruction error, with default alpha = 0.8.

claim_text: In BOND's Weibo data a user is labelled suspicious if the user made at least five suspicious events (determined from temporal information); suspicious users are the outliers, and timestamps were not used to build features.
BOND's Weibo graph is a directed user-user graph linking users who used the same hashtag, with 400-d features (100 location + 300 text dimensions).
BOND's Reddit graph is a user-subreddit graph in which banned users are treated as outliers; subreddit nodes are not labelled anomalous.

On Weibo the outliers show both structural and contextual properties (clustering coefficient 0.400 vs 0.301; neighbour feature similarity 0.004 vs 0.993), while Reddit outliers look like inliers on these measures.

claim_text: In the Independent Cascade model a newly active node v gets one chance to activate each inactive neighbour w with probability p_vw, independently of history; success makes w active at the next step and v never retries.

Influence maximisation under Independent Cascade is NP-hard (hard to approximate better than 1 - 1/e), while the spread function is monotone and submodular so greedy selection gives a (1 - 1/e - epsilon) approximation when spread is estimated by simulation.

Computing the expected spread sigma(A) exactly is #P-complete and is approximated by Monte-Carlo simulation; Kempe et al. used 10,000 simulations per seed set and compared greedy with degree centrality, distance centrality and random choice.
Kempe, Kleinberg, Tardos appeared at KDD 2003, pp. 137-146 (doi 10.1145/956750.956769); the journal version is Theory of Computing 11(4):105-147, 2015.
source_location: Reference [51] of the journal version; ToC front page

claim_text: Akoglu, Tong and Koutra's survey organises graph anomaly detection by unsupervised vs (semi-)supervised, static vs dynamic and attributed vs plain graphs, and stresses anomaly attribution (explaining why a node is anomalous).
Brandes and Pich estimate shortest-path centralities from a limited number of single-source computations and study how source-selection strategy affects accuracy.

MADAN (Gutierrez-Gomez et al., AAAI 2020) restricts itself to undirected, connected, simple graphs, weights edges by Gaussian attribute similarity and uses heat-kernel smoothing across scales; it was evaluated on Disney, Books and Enron plus synthetic networks.

GNNExplainer learns a sigmoid-mapped edge mask and a feature mask by maximising mutual information with the prediction, and was evaluated by explanation accuracy against ground-truth motifs on synthetic graphs.

The GNNExplainer paper states that GAT attention values are the same for predictions across all nodes, so they cannot give per-instance explanations, and its attention baseline (average attention across layers) performed poorly.
In NLP, Jain and Wallace found attention weights often disagree with gradient-based importance and that different attention distributions can give the same predictions.

Wiegreffe and Pinter argue that whether attention is an explanation depends on the definition of explanation and propose four tests, concluding the earlier result does not rule out attention being useful.
A 2024 preprint reports that attention-based GNN interpretations (GAT, Graph Transformers) can be unstable under perturbations such as added edges or nodes.

GraphXAI reports existing explainers perform considerably worse on heterophilic and attributed graphs and measures faithfulness by keeping the top-k features and comparing predictions with a KL-based score.

DeepLinker/GANR define 'Attention Rank' as the sum, over heads of the second layer and over neighbours, of normalised attention coefficients directed at a node, and report it outperforming PageRank, closeness and betweenness on a venture-capital and an APS citation network.
source_location: arXiv Sec. 4.3, Eq. 7, Table 4; Sci. Rep. page

claim_text: AnomalyDAE puts attention in its structure encoder and scores nodes by attribute and structure reconstruction error; ResGCN uses a residual-based attention to reduce the influence of anomalous nodes.

claim_text: GCOMB, DeepIM and ToupleGDD use GNN encoders to learn influence-maximisation seed selection and do not address anomaly detection.

claim_text: A 2025 paper uses average controllability, a node-influence measure, as an input weight or feature to improve GNN anomaly detection.

In the searches performed no paper was found that jointly produces an influence ranking and an anomaly score from one GNN encoder, or that scores anomalies by received attention; this is a statement about the search, not proof of absence.
This work is the first unified influence-and-anomaly GNN with a novel architecture.
